articles.title: AGENT RELIABILITY PATTERNS: ON-DEMAND GUIDES
articles.summary: Almost right, but not quite is developers' most-cited AI frustration in Stack Overflow's 2025 survey, and it stops being tolerable once AI agents handle production work. The shift reaches ordinary AI features too. Anything that chains model calls into multi-step work inherits the same failure classes.

articles.title: THE FIVE COMPONENTS OF BUILDING A "COMPANY HARNESS"
articles.summary: LangChain's internal agents share five components: Slack interfaces, scoped credentials, shared and personal memory, sandboxed execution, and scheduled runs. Memory remains the least solved piece.

articles.title: CLAUDE CODE SKILLS FOR TEAMS: WHAT TO MOVE OUT OF CLAUDE.MD
articles.summary: Keep always-needed rules in CLAUDE.md and move task-specific procedures into skills that load on demand. Restrict deployment and other side-effecting skills to manual use, with reviewed tool permissions.

articles.title: HOW META BUILT FORUM WITH AI-NATIVE ENGINEERING
articles.summary: Meta built Forum by having agents plan, implement, test, and correct changes while engineers set goals and approved results. A small team reached Facebook Groups feature parity in eight weeks.

articles.title: HUNGER BEATS TENURE: ADVICE FOR JUNIOR ENGINEERS
articles.summary: Junior engineers can gain influence by building one focused prototype tied to a business goal. Fresh eyes help challenge assumptions that experienced teammates have stopped questioning.

articles.title: ARE FIXED USER FLOWS BECOMING OBSOLETE?
articles.summary: Intent-driven UX adapts flows to a user's goal, context, and behavior. Designers define the rules and boundaries, including confirmations, undo, and fallbacks when the system misreads intent.

articles.title: AI PROMISED LESS WORK. I HAVE NEVER WORKED MORE
articles.summary: Cheaper implementation makes more projects worth starting, but reviewing agent output and switching contexts still consume attention. A personal GitHub activity analysis traces cycles of increased output and burnout as that workload grows.

articles.summary: Expo's experimental CLI helps agents choose the right build, launch an app, and smoke-test it. Structured output and runtime inspection help agents diagnose failures.

articles.title: APPLE INTRODUCES THE 14-INCH MACBOOK PRO WITH M6
articles.summary: The new 14-inch MacBook Pro adds a 12-core CPU and GPU, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 6. Apple claims up to 30% faster Xcode builds than M5. The new laptop will be available starting on November 6.

articles.title: TABLETOP WHALE
articles.summary: Tabletop Whale explains science, from ventilation to lunar geology, through animations, illustrations, and maps. Several projects have shared their source data or code.

articles.title: HOW APPLE FITS AN LLM ON YOUR IPHONE
articles.summary: Apple fits a 3-billion-parameter model on the iPhone using compressed weights, shared caches, and small task-specific adapters. More complex requests go to Private Cloud Compute.

articles.summary: Next.js plans fixes for seven medium-severity vulnerabilities on November 3.
